subject: Spectra preview: request for temporary latency safety net
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@novumhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spectra preview: request for temporary latency safety net

Hi team,

Following the Novum Health onboarding call this morning I want to request a short, scoped SLA adjustment for the Spectra preview we're running for them. The heart of the ask: allow a temporary 95th-percentile latency tolerance of +250ms above our published preview SLO for a 14-day pilot window while we validate a new attention kernel and a sequence-length-aware batching policy.

Why: Novum's integration has a skew toward long context (avg 1.8k tokens) and our current Spectra kernel shows higher variance at those lengths. We've rolled an instrumented build to a subset of hosts; early telemetry (attached) shows tail spikes during multi-tenant peak periods.

Impact: this would be a customer-facing exception (preview tier only), limited to Novum's route and two test model revisions. No change to uptime commitments — only a temporary softening of the latency SLO for this route so the product team can iterate without triggering automated downgrade/fallbacks.

Requested guardrails:
- Duration: 14 calendar days starting 2027-05-03 (timezone: PST)
- Scope: Novum Health route only (route id in HS-12934), Spectra preview model variants v0.9 and v0.9.1
- Observability: infra will publish per-route 99/95/50 percentile dashboards and will alert us on error-rate > 0.5% or sustained p95 > published + 500ms
- Rollback: auto-revert to standard SLO at end of window unless an extension is approved by Product + Infra + Sales.

Attached: spectra-latency-report.pdf (summary) and a small sample CSV with per-request latencies.

Ask: Lauren/Markus — approval needed by EOD tomorrow so Sales can confirm with Novum. Aditya — please confirm that Novum will accept the temporary guardrail and that we can proceed with the pilot if approved.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@novumhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spectra preview: request for temporary latency safety net

Connor —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple quick clarifying Qs: is Novum on Dedicated or Hosted preview? My recollection was Hosted preview but that affects whether we can isolate their route (routing/fallback policies differ). Also, can you confirm whether the latency variance correlates with any particular prompt types?

If it's Hosted, I want infra to confirm that we won't be exposing other customers to increased tail by making any config changes.

Happy to fast-track this if Markus signs off.

- Lauren
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@novumhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spectra preview: request for temporary latency safety net

Quick infra readout:
- Novum is on Hosted preview (confirmed).
- We can apply a per-route latency guard that prevents automated fallback to lower-cost model variants; that will keep their traffic on the instrumented hosts.
- The observed spikes are correlated with long-sequence (>1.5k tokens) batched requests and a kernel codepath that is not yet quantization-optimized.
- Risk: during cross-tenant peak windows there is a measurable tail increase for co-hosted tenants; mitigations are: temporary isolation of Novum's traffic to a small dedicated pool (no SLA change to uptime), or enable the safety net while leaving routing as-is but with tighter error-rate monitoring.

I endorse the safety-net with the following conditions:
1) We spin up an isolated pilot pool (2 hosts) for Novum's route for the 14-day window — infra will bear the incremental cost but we need Product sign-off.
2) Instrumented tracing and a short runbook for rollback must be in place (I'll own the runbook).
3) We block any routing changes that increase exposure for other customers.

If Product + Sales are OK with the pilot pool cost, infra can have this in place by Monday morning.

- Markus
Director, Infrastructure

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 09:29 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@novumhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spectra preview: request for temporary latency safety net

Connor/Team —

Novum is fine with the proposed guardrails. I spoke with Maria after the call; they understand this is a preview and are comfortable with a temporary latency allowance as long as: (a) we commit to daily updates during the 14 days, and (b) any customer-impacting errors trigger an immediate rollback.

Sales is okay to absorb the pilot pool cost for the first week; if the pool needs to persist beyond 7 days we will discuss cost-sharing with Novum (HS-12934 has the note).

Please confirm timelines and I will inform the customer and update the mutual action plan.

- Aditya
Account Executive

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 11:04 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@novumhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spectra preview: request for temporary latency safety net

Hi Connor / Aditya —

Thanks for the transparency and the proposed plan. Novum accepts the temporary latency safety net and the guardrails as described. We appreciate the pilot pool offer and the daily updates — please include any notable regression examples in the daily digest so our engineers can triage quickly.

A couple asks from our side: if you hit any errors that materially affect correctness (not just latency), we want an immediate notification and a freeze on any further model-side changes until we align. Also, can you include a short summary of the mitigation timeline in the mutual action plan?

Looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Maria Garcia
Director of AI Integrations
Novum Health

---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spectra preview: request for temporary latency safety net

Maria —

Thanks for the quick confirmation and the asks — all noted. Action items and timeline:
- 2027-05-03 07:00 PST: Infra will bring up the isolated 2-host pilot pool and route Novum traffic there (Markus will announce when complete).
- Daily: Connor will publish a short latency digest to HS-12934 and share any notable regressions; infra will provide per-route dashboards.
- Immediate: any correctness-impacting errors -> immediate notification + freeze on model changes until a joint triage.
- 2027-05-17 07:00 PST: Pilot window end; Product will recommend continue/rollback/modify.

I've attached the latency report and a sample CSV for your engineering team. We'll send the first digest tomorrow EOD PST.

If that aligns, Aditya — please update the mutual action plan and confirm in HubSpot.

Cheers,
Connor
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: spectra-latency-report.pdf (summary of telemetry), spectra-preview-latency-sample.csv (sample rows).
